newsitem.title: CANADA: Taiwan sailors in stowaway case to leave Canada.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan sailors in stowaway case to leave Canada.

text.p: Six Taiwanese sailors accused of sending three Romanian stowaways overboard to their deaths on the high seas will be allowed to leave Canada, Canadian Justice Minister Allan Rock said on Tuesday.
In a statement from Ottawa, Rock said the seamen, all officers of the merchant ship Maersk Dubai, were expected to leave Canada on Thursday to face prosecution in Taiwan.

Rock said the decision to send the Taiwese sailors home was made after Taiwanese authorities gave Canada assurances that the evidence would be fully reviewed and the men would face prosecution in Taipei for their alleged crimes.

Earlier this month, Nova Scotia Supreme Court Judge Michael MacDonald freed the sailors after ruling that he did not have the authority to order their extradition to Romania on murder charges. The officers were not allowed to leave Canada, pending an appeal.
In his ruling, MacDonald said enough evidence was presented during a 41-day extradition hearing last autumn to warrant murder and manslaughter charges against the seamen.

Rock said that in allowing the officers to return to Taiwan, the Canadian government would abandon its attempt to overturn MacDonald's decision to free the men. "Pursuing an appeal is both uncertain and lengthy," Rock said.

"The fundamental objective of the government of Canada has been throughout to bring these individuals, if found responsible for these alleged crimes, to justice as expeditiously as possible," he said.

Duncan Beveridge, a lawyer for one of the accused officers, told Reuters that Rock's decision to send the officers back to Taiwan was "good and practical" and "they should have been returned there from the start."
The officers have been part of a year-long diplomatic tussle between Canada, Romania, Taiwan and the People's Republic of China.

Acting on behalf of Romania, Canada was seeking to extradite the officers to Bucharest. Taiwan opposed the extradition and finally offered to prosecute the men in Taipei. Meanwhile, Beijing claimed sovereignty over both.

The Filipino sailors who abandoned the Maersk Dubai in this port city on Canada's Atlantic cost last May to accuse the ship's captain and officers of murder on the high seas will be encouraged to testify in Taiwan, he said.

During the Canadian extradition hearing, the Filipino sailors testified that the Taiwanese officers put two Romanian stowaways overboard to their presumed deaths off the Spanish coast in March 1996. On another voyage in May, a Romanian stowaway on the ship was also put overboard, they said.
The missing stowaways' bodies were never found, and authorities in Bucharest said the men's families have not heard from the Romanians.
